title: Phasing Heuristics and Telemetry Sentinel - Weekplan (Oct 2026) - Proposal
content:
Purpose:
This working draft defines: a) phasing heuristics for multi-stage rollouts (percent-based corridors), b) a compact weekly launch plan for a typical feature change, and c) the telemetry sentinel (signal thresholds + annotation matrix) we use as preflight and live-release gates. Aim: give on-call / release shepherds a deterministic, low-friction playbook that reduces guesswork during scale-ups and provides clear rollback triggers.

High-level phasing heuristics (intent):
- Phase naming: seed -> micro-canary -> ramp1 -> ramp2 -> steady -> global. Keep phases short and observable.
- Percent steps: seed (0.1%), micro-canary (1%), ramp1 (5%), ramp2 (20%), steady (60-100% depending on risk profile).
- Minimum dwell time per phase: 15 minutes for seed/micro, 30–60 minutes for ramps, 2–4 hours for steady before further business-driven expansion.
- Traffic conditioning: only route new traffic; do not migrate in-flight long-running sessions during early ramps.
- Auto-rollback window: configured per-service; default is 15m for micro-canary, 30m for ramp1, 60m for ramp2.
- Burst tolerance: allow brief tolerance for spike-like metric blips if they resolve within 3 consecutive datapoints (1 datapoint = 1 minute by default).

Signal prioritization (primary -> secondary):
- Primary (immediate rollback candidates): 5xx rate increase (absolute + relative), p99 latency regression beyond SLO threshold, model error rate (crash/invalid tokens), major downstream quota errors.
- Secondary (investigate / hold expansion): sustained CPU/GPU contention, memory pressure > 80% on serving nodes, degraded cache hit rate > 15% drop, increased tail latency on specific path (e.g., embeddings).
- Tertiary (postmortem signals): user-reported quality regressions, subtle semantic drift (requires eval harness), small cost-per-token increases.

Compact telemetry sentinel (threshold examples; tune per-service):
- 5xx errors: absolute > 0.5% OR 3x baseline over 5m -> immediate rollback.
- p99 latency: > 2x SLO and > 1s above historical baseline in 5m window -> hold/rollback.
- CPU/GPU saturation: > 90% for 10m -> hold and investigate.
- KV cache miss rate: sudden +20 percentage points drop vs baseline -> investigate caching config/fallbacks.
- Memory OOMs: any OOM observed -> immediate rollback and nodes quarantined.

Change Annotation Matrix (for release notes and ops):
- Category: infra change / model change / config / schema / routing-policy
- Impact tag: low | medium | high | data-sensitive
- Risk mitigations: circuit-breaker, canary-percent, automatic-fallback-model, read-only gating
- Required docs: runbook link, key dashboards, git PR, test coverage note

Example annotation row (freeform):
- infra change; medium; autoscaler rewrite -> mitigation: seed 0.1%, add manual throttle; dashboards: infra/autoscale; PR: #2897; test: load-test-coverage 80%.

Weekly launch plan (compact template) - Week 0 (owner = release-shepherd):
- Mon: Finalize change annotation matrix; confirm linked PRs + test recipients. Dry-run smoke in staging (10k tokens/day simulated).
- Tue: Canary config baked; infra changes merged but feature-flagged. Post-merge small smoke.
- Wed: Seed deploy at 09:00 PST (0.1%) -> monitor 2 hours. If green, micro-canary at 11:30 (1%).
- Thu: Ramp1 (5%) at 10:00 -> hold 60m, evaluate sentinel. Ramp2 (20%) at 14:00 if stable.
- Fri: Steady (60%) at 10:00, business decision for global. Release-notes draft circulated to PM/CS.
- Sat/Sun: Quiet window; only emergency fixes. On-call rotation active.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- PRs merged + green CI (unit + integration + smoke).
- Load test snapshot: 95th/99th latencies within 10% of baseline.
- Dashboards: release snapshot created; alert runbook linked.
- Backfills / migrations: dry-run completed.
- Backout plan: validated rollback-priorities and version pins.
- Stakeholders notified: PM, SRE, Customer Success, Legal (if data-sensitive).

Live rollout checklist (during each phase):
- Confirm routing policy applied to correct region/tier.
- Watch primary sentinel dashboard for 15m. Note anomalies with timestamp and probable root cause tag.
- If primary signal fires: engage on-call, flip immediate rollback toggle, notify release channel with template comment (phase, signal, action).
- If secondary signal fires: pause expansion, open investigation thread, maintain current phase for at least 30m.

Rollback play (fast path):
- Toggle route back to previous stable model/service version.
- Mark nodes as quarantined (SRE action).
- Create incident stub with minimal info: summary, phase, top signal, initial mitigation.
- Notify: #release-channel, stakeholders, and customer-exposed comms if >5% user impact.

Release notes - draft (to be copied to CHANGELOG + release email):
Title: Controlled rollout: autoscaler and model-serving config update
Date: 2026-10-08
Summary: This release updates the autoscaler logic to reduce cold-starts and improves model-serving memory isolation. Expected benefits: lower cold-start latency and fewer noisy restarts under burst traffic. No schema changes.
Impact: Customers should see improved tail latency for short sessions; no action required. Data handling: no change in telemetry retention or export.
Known limitations: If your workload has extreme per-request memory variance, enable per-tenant memory caps (config in Console).
Contact: customer-success@redwood.ai for escalation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we make the seed dwell time configurable by service (current default 15m)? Pros: faster feedback. Cons: higher flakiness for very noisy endpoints.
- Decide whether to include cost-telemetry gating as a hard gate for ramp2.
- Add automated annotation of thermalized signals to Jira when triggered.

Appendix: quick ops snippets
- Canary rollback CLI: rtx release rollback --service {svc} --version {prev} --reason "sentinel:5xx"
- Snapshot creation: rtx snapshot create --dashboard release/{release-id}
- Channel notify template: [RELEASE-ID] phase={phase} action={action} summary={short-reason} link={dash_url}

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally compact — prefer references to the larger runbooks (confluence links above) rather than duplicating long instructions. We'll iterate the thresholds after the next three rollouts (measure false-positive / false-negative gating rates).
